title: KV cache shard hotspot: fairness, backpressure and memory drain audit
creator: Maya Chen
description: Post-incident audit following a multi-tenant KV cache capacity event where asymmetric shard hotspots and an intermittent compaction stall caused uneven eviction scoring, transient tenant memory growth, and degraded tail latency for affected customers. This ticket tracks investigation findings, proposed mitigations, rollouts, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence and to improve observability.
timeline: 2026-02-20 03:18 UTC: First alert - elevated memory pressure on kvcache-shard-17 and tail latency spike observed in dashboard (dash:kv/2026-02-20)
2026-02-20 03:22 UTC: Automated fallback triggered to pad shards; partial recovery observed but eviction oscillation began
2026-02-20 05:10 UTC: Incident declared; SRE and kvcache owners paged and Slack channel #inc-2026-kvcache-hotspot created
2026-02-20 09:30 UTC: Initial mitigation - increased eviction aggressiveness globally, which reduced latency but caused collateral eviction for low-traffic tenants
2026-02-21 to 2026-02-27: Root cause analysis and forensic runs using kvcache-replay harness; found correlated compaction pauses with shard-local decay factor misapplication
root_cause_summary: A race between the async slab compaction job and the eviction-score decay path allowed a shard to temporarily under-decay its eviction scores. Combined with a bursty tenant access pattern, this produced a hotspot where entries were not aged correctly, bypassing tenant-weight caps and leading to a local memory surge. A secondary contributing factor was insufficient telemetry around per-shard score distributions and backpressure signals, so the cascade was not visible until tail latency degraded.
decisions: 1) Implement a shard-local eviction-score normalization step to ensure decay is applied deterministically before any eviction decision (decision made 2026-02-25)
2) Add a per-tenant soft slab quota and hard watermark that triggers adaptive eviction backpressure instead of global eviction changes (approved 2026-02-26)
3) Deploy a targeted canary for AEB (Adaptive Eviction Backpressure) on 10% of shards in prod, evaluate for 72 hours, then expand (plan 2026-03-05)
4) Instrument new telemetry and alerts for shard score skew, compaction pause duration, and tenant slab utilization (2026-02-28)
5) Update runbook to include an automated shard-reshard operation and recommended thresholds for manual intervention (2026-03-02)
action_items: A1: Implement deterministic decay ordering inside eviction path and add unit + fuzz tests (owner: Ravi Patel, estimate: 3)
A2: Prototype and ship per-tenant soft quota + hard watermark; surface metrics (owner: Leila Gómez, estimate: 5)
A3: Build AEB feature to emit backpressure signals to request router and throttler; add integration tests with canary harness (owner: Tom Hsu, estimate: 8)
A4: Create shard heatmap dashboard (per-shard score distribution, compaction pause histogram, tenant-watermark breaches) and a runbook page (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2)
A5: Author regression test using kvcache-replay with synthetic skewed-access traces and include in CI gating for runtime-1.22 (owner: Maya Chen, estimate: 3)
A6: Roll out AEB to canary cohort and run 72-hour soak; collect memory, latency, and tenant-impact metrics; decision gate for wider rollout (owner: Release Eng, due: 2026-03-12)
A7: Notify enterprise customers in the affected set with a summary and mitigations; coordinate SOC/CS with messaging template (owner: Customer Ops, due: 2026-03-03)
A8: Postmortem writeup and Q&A session for platform + SRE teams; include learnings in onboarding doc (owner: Incident Lead, due: 2026-03-05)
notes: 2026-02-24: SRE flagged that global eviction tuning was causing increased eviction churn for small tenants; this influenced the decision to prefer per-tenant quotas instead of global tuning.
2026-02-26: Design review with PD and Security - per-tenant quotas do not change data isolation guarantees; security approved earlier than expected.
2026-03-01: UX/PM asked for a customer-facing metric summary; added an 'affected-tenants' export in the dashboard workstream.
2026-03-04: Engineering review - concern about additional CPU cost from AEB signals; mitigation: implement lightweight sampling and aggregate signals at shard-level before routing.
2026-03-08: QA found a rare timing bug in the replay harness; fixed in PR 14233 and re-ran regression suite
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic decay ordering implemented and covered by unit + fuzz tests
Per-tenant soft quotas in prod with metrics showing reduced cross-tenant eviction bleed (target: 90% fewer cross-tenant evictions during skewed loads)
AEB canary runs for 72 hours with no customer-visible regressions and acceptable CPU overhead (<5% increased systime on shard hosts)
New dashboards and alerts deployed with playbook entries and an automated shim to reshuffle overloaded shards
Incident postmortem published and communicated to affected customers
